Subject: Forecast health check — prune stale items and confirm commit by EOD

Team —

Quick, targeted ask as we close this week’s commit window: finance pulled a forecast health export (attached) and there are ~18 opportunities flagged with no activity in 90+ days or with close dates that slid twice without updated next steps. We need to clean these up so the commit reflects realistic upside.

Please do the following by EOD today:
- For any opp with no contact in 90+ days, either update next step + close date OR move to Disqualified/No-Commit (use the "No Commit" reason code)
- If an opp still has active engagement, update Stage, Probability and a one-line Next Step in the Notes field (this is what finance uses to validate commits)
- If you think an opportunity should remain in commit despite staleness, mark it with a clear justification in the Notes and tag me (Sean)

I attached the SFDC export filtered to deals in the current quarter. Link to the Forecast Health report is below if you want to triage there instead. Finance will take the updated snapshot at 5pm PT and push numbers to the weekly model, so changes need to be made before then.

Attachments: sfdc_export_20270515.csv (CSV, 34KB)
Related report: https://redwood-salesforce.example.com/report/ForecastHealthMay2027

Thanks — concise updates are fine, I mostly need stage/close-date/probability + next step.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Director, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference

Thanks Sean — quick clarifying Qs before I dive in:
1) Threshold — you said 90+ days for no contact. Should we also treat any opportunity with a close date earlier than today and no activity in 30 days as stale?
2) Move vs No-Commit — if a deal is still technically "working" but we've missed two forecast commits and there's no scheduled exec call, should we move to Disqualified or keep as "No Commit (internal)"? Finance prefers Disqualified for true dead deals.
3) Do you want us to bulk-change stage to "No Commit" or add a custom field value? I can make the bulk updates but want to align on the label so reporting stays consistent.

I'll start with the named accounts (I see three for Acme) and update notes as I go.

—Laura
